stem:
Tushar has two $5$ cm by $1$ cm rectangles. He joins them along a shared $1$ cm edge and asks how the perimeter changes.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: The joined perimeter is the area $10$ square centimetres of the joined strip.
The joined perimeter is $12+12=24$ cm, the sum of the separate perimeters.
The joined perimeter is $22$ cm, because the two touching $1$ cm edges are inside and not on the outside boundary.
The new outside boundary is what creates the two separate $5$ cm by $1$ cm rectangles.

teacher.key_rationale: Each strip has perimeter 12 cm. Joining along 1 cm removes 2 cm from the boundary, so the outside perimeter is 22 cm (a 10 by 1 rectangle). Calling perimeter the area swaps terms. Keeping 24 omits that touching edges leave the boundary. Saying the new boundary creates the separate pieces reverses the cut-and-join relation.
